uncited: Rendering Implementation defines the computational pipeline that transforms a set of 3D Gaussian primitives into a 2D image.
It solves the problem of efficiently evaluating the volume rendering equation for explicit, particle-based scene representations by leveraging hardware-accelerated rasterization .

It sets itself apart from its siblings by providing the foundational mechanisms—specifically the projection from 3D covariance to 2D screen-space conics and the alpha compositing logic—that enable both the high-performance GPU rasterization of [3D Gaussian Splatting](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) and the display-only CPU-sorted instancing of [3D Gaussian Splatting Rendering (CPU-Sorted, Instanced)](2058-3d-gaussian-splatting-rendering-cpu-sorted-instanced.md).
*   Scale $s$ is exponentiated to ensure positivity: $s_{eff} = \exp(s)$ [Parent].

*   The 3D covariance matrix is constructed as $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{3D} = \mathbf{R} \mathbf{S} \mathbf{S}^T \mathbf{R}^T$, where $\mathbf{R}$ is the rotation matrix derived from $q_{norm}$ and $\mathbf{S} = \text{diag}(s_{eff})$ [Parent].
*   The mean position is transformed to camera space: $\boldsymbol{\mu}' = \mathbf{V} \boldsymbol{\mu}$ [Parent].
*   Early termination occurs when $T$ drops below a threshold (e.g., 0.05) [Parent].

The rendering pipeline originates from the 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework, which introduced explicit Gaussian primitives to replace volumetric ray marching for real-time novel view synthesis .
The method was developed to overcome the computational cost of NeRFs while maintaining high visual fidelity .
The specific projection and rasterization techniques described here are standard implementations of the 3DGS rendering equation .
